verses.text: Look, a king will reign doing what’s right, and his officials will rule with justice.
A man will be like a shelter from the wind, a hiding place from the storm, streams in a dry place, or a huge rock throwing shade in a worn-out land.
The eyes of those who see won’t be dim, and people with ears to hear will actually listen.
People who rush in without thinking will come to understand, and people who stammer will be ready to speak clearly.
Nobody will call the fool noble anymore, and nobody will treat the cheat like someone worth looking up to.
The fool talks nonsense and plans wrong in his heart. He treats holy things with contempt, says false things about the LORD, leaves hungry people empty, and keeps thirsty people from getting a drink.
The cheat’s methods are rotten. He makes wicked plans to ruin humble people with lies, even when someone in need is telling the truth.
But people of honor make honorable plans, and they stick with what’s honorable.
Get up, you women taking it easy! Hear my voice! You daughters without a care, listen to what I’m saying!
In a little over a year, you carefree women will be shaken. The grapes will fail. The harvest won’t come.
Shake, you women taking it easy! Be troubled, you carefree ones! Strip down and tie sackcloth around your waist.
Beat your chests for those beautiful fields and the vines that used to be full of fruit.
Thorns and briars will push up on my people’s land. Yes, they’ll cover every house that used to be full of laughter in that happy city.
The palace will be abandoned. The bustling city will empty out. The hill and watchtower will become dens forever, a happy place for wild donkeys and a pasture for flocks,
until the Spirit is poured out on us from above. Then the wilderness will become a fruitful field, and people will call that fruitful field a forest.
Justice will live in the wilderness, and righteousness will stay in the fruitful field.
Doing what’s right will produce peace, and the result of righteousness will be quiet and confidence forever.
My people will live where there’s peace, in safe homes and quiet spots to rest,
even when hail flattens the forest and the city is leveled to the ground.
Blessed are you who sow beside every stream and let the ox and donkey go out freely.
